_about: Paper Cinema shot library: named, reusable camera moves for KUROKO (main engine, shot.rig) and the motion page (film.camera beats). Read docs/DIRECTION.md and .claude/skills/scene-direction/SKILL.md. Marks: D = documented in our own docs/tests, C = commonly reported (secondary sources), I = our inference.
_how_to_paste: Main engine: copy 'rig' (tuned for 9:16 vertical, the default format) or 'rig_16x9' (when present, for horizontal films) into a shot: {"id":"S3","start":4.6,"end":6.2,"mode":"dawn","rig": <rig>}. Replace 'hero'/'foe' with your performer ids (parts: .head .chest .hips .hand .root).
Anchor rigs: beat 't' values here are seconds FROM THE SHOT START; add shot.start to each before pasting (the checker requires absolute times inside the shot).
Motion page (film/motion-test.json style): copy 'beat' into film.camera; 't' (and slide 'until') are absolute seconds: set them to your times. 'who' is the cast id.
'pair' = two rigs for the two sides of a cut (shot A, then shot B).
Style 'fx' ids and 'grade' moods refer to library/effects.json and engine/fx.js MOODS (status there: built / new / planned).

Every rig here was run through engine/validate.mjs and through KUROKO (engine/kuroko.js) against the film/kuroko-duel.json choreography in 9:16 and 16:9 on 2026-11-23: none loses its main subject. 'measured' = the far subject's body height as % of frame height and its margin (1 = centre, 0 = frame edge). Motion-page 'beat' objects follow film/motion-test.json but were not render-tested. The blade rig needs the live blade frame (main engine only).

units.duration_s: seconds (24 fps; frames_24 = the same in frames)
units.angle: frame rig: degrees off profile, + toward subject[0]'s back; orbit deg = world azimuth

lens_equivalents._about: fov -> full-frame lens. 9:16 uses the 36 mm side (rotated camera); 16:9 uses a 20.25 mm tall 16:9 crop.

shots.name: Establishing wide
shots.purpose: Show place, time and both fighters as small shapes in the world.
shots.when: First 2-4 s of the fight body, or after the hook. Once per film.

shots.name: Crane reveal
shots.purpose: Start close and low, rise and pull back to reveal the setting and the opponent.
shots.when: Opening of a scene or the end of an aftermath. Hides information then pays it off.
shots.notes: Anchor beat t values are seconds from the shot start: add shot.start before pasting. Crane spring (0.7 Hz) takes about 1 s to arrive, so give the shot at least 2.5 s.

shots.name: Silhouette wide (profile)
shots.purpose: Two black shapes against a bright sky: pure pose and distance, no detail.
shots.when: Standoff, the moment before the decisive blow, or the hook frame. Strong in thumbnails.
shots.elevation: 0 deg (eye level, horizon low in frame)
shots.notes: Profile is the only angle where both poses read as clean outlines. Light from behind (sun or backdrop glow), no front fill. In vertical the profile makes the pair small: use it as a held graphic beat, not as coverage.

shots.name: Telephoto weather wide (Kurosawa)
shots.purpose: Long-lens view through moving weather (wind, rain, paper snow, mist): the fighters stacked and compressed in layers.
shots.when: World beat or standoff; any shot that needs 'nature is watching'.
shots.distance: far (frame rig puts the camera 2-3x further back at this fov)
shots.notes: Long lens compresses depth so fore/background layers feel stacked. Needs moving weather particles in the set (not built in the browser set: wind lines, paper snow). [C] Kurosawa: long lens + multiple cameras from Seven Samurai on; weather in nearly every film.

shots.name: One-point symmetry
shots.purpose: Camera on the duel axis, horizon centred, the fighters stacked on the vanishing point: order, inevitability, unease.
shots.when: Arrival down a path, a formal bow, the frame before a death. Once per film at most.
shots.notes: The frame rig clamps angle at 75. For an exact axis view use an orbit with deg0 = deg1 pointing down the duel line (in our sets the line runs along z: deg 0 or 180), radius 4-6, height 0. Symmetric set dressing matters more than the camera.

shots.name: Small in the dark (final full body)
shots.purpose: One figure small in a sea of black, lit by a single source.
shots.when: Last shot before the end card; after a monologue.
shots.notes: From research/reference-videos.md video C. Use the studio mode or a night set; the figure's inner lantern glow is the brightest thing on screen.

shots.name: Eye reveal
shots.purpose: Slow drift on the eyes; lids open or the glow rises on a beat.
shots.when: Hook (first second), before the draw, before any decisive strike.
shots.distance: head fills the frame, eyes on the upper third
shots.notes: Motion-page beat aims at the real eye joint; the KUROKO face rig aims at the head. Pair with eye glow 'anticipation' 2.2 and a 'decide' flare 3.5 for one frame (docs/FIX-LIST.md).

shots.name: Extreme close-up eyes (Leone)
shots.purpose: Only the eyes, edge to edge. Intercut with the other fighter's eyes, getting closer each cut.
shots.when: Standoff build-up, 3-6 alternating inserts before the strike.
shots.distance: extreme close: eye strip ~20 cm wide
shots.notes: Each inter-cut gets tighter (dist 0.6 -> 0.5 -> 0.42) and shorter (1.5 s -> 1.0 -> 0.6). Alternate hero/foe. Silence or one sustained note under it. [C] Leone: extreme long shot vs extreme close-up, moving closer to the eyes on every cut.

shots.name: Over-the-shoulder standoff
shots.purpose: Near fighter's shoulder and blade in the foreground, opponent framed beyond: depth staging for 9:16.
shots.when: The default two-shot in vertical. Dialogue, sizing-up, the step before an attack.
shots.emotion: confrontation, threat seen through the hero's eyes
shots.distance: full on the far fighter (>= 45% frame height)
shots.notes: docs/FIX-LIST.md: OTS 55-68 deg is the vertical fix. The first subject is the near (shoulder) fighter.

shots.name: Reverse over-the-shoulder
shots.purpose: The matching reverse: over the opponent's shoulder onto the hero, same side of the line.
shots.when: Cut back and forth with over-shoulder-standoff (shot / reverse shot).
shots.notes: Negative angle swings toward subject[1]'s back on the SAME side of the line, so screen direction holds (180-degree rule). Keep fov and elevation equal to the forward OTS so the pair matches.

shots.name: Standoff orbit
shots.purpose: Slow arc around both fighters as they circle: builds pressure without cutting.
shots.when: Opening of the standoff, 2-4 s; the camera circles, the fighters do not move much.
shots.angle: sweeps 50 deg of world azimuth on one side of the line
shots.notes: Orbit degrees are WORLD azimuth (0 = camera on +z of the target). Our sets stage the duel line along z, so keep both deg0 and deg1 inside (-180, 0) for the x<0 side or (0, 180) for x>0. Speed: 10-20 deg/s reads as deliberate; > 40 deg/s reads as action.

shots.name: Profile two-shot (the line)
shots.purpose: Both fighters side-on, the gap between them is the subject.
shots.when: Standoff hold, measuring distance, the Sanjuro-style frozen moment.
shots.notes: In 9:16 a profile two-shot leaves the fighters small (separation fills the narrow width). Prefer it for horizontal films, or as one held graphic beat in vertical.

shots.name: Telephoto compression two-shot
shots.purpose: Long lens makes the gap between the fighters look shorter than it is: they seem nose to nose.
shots.when: Just before the charge; makes a 3 m gap feel like no gap.
shots.notes: Lens compression [C]. Handheld noise is scaled by fov, so even 'locked' is safest at this focal length.

shots.name: Slow push-in (monologue)
shots.purpose: A barely visible push toward one figure while it speaks or breathes; 2-5% closer per second.
shots.when: Under a voice line, a vow, the dark-monologue Shorts format.
shots.notes: Beat t relative to shot start. The crane spring turns the step at 0.5 s into a ~1.5 s glide; for a longer push add more beats every 1 s, each 4-6% closer (dist 0.82, 0.78, 0.74...). From research/reference-videos.md: push-in 2-5% per second.

shots.name: Hand-on-hilt insert
shots.purpose: Tight insert on the hand tightening on the tsuka, thumb pushing the tsuba (koiguchi).
shots.when: 6-10 frames before a draw or a strike; the cut that says 'now'.
shots.angle: 60 (front-side; 0 would put the camera on the duel line, behind the opponent)
shots.notes: docs/FIX-LIST.md: 6-10 frame inserts (eyes, hand tightening, foot grinding) before each strike. Sync the koiguchi click to the first frame.

shots.name: Foot-grind insert
shots.purpose: Low insert of the lead foot sliding forward or grinding into sand.
shots.when: Just before a lunge; replaces a wind-up you cannot see in a tight frame.
shots.notes: The ground guard keeps the camera above 0.15 m. Add a sand/paper-dust puff and a cloth-scuff sound.

shots.name: Low hero push
shots.purpose: Camera near the ground looking up, pushing in: the fighter towers.
shots.when: Hero's resolve, a power-up, the winner standing after the blow.
shots.notes: docs/FIX-LIST.md camera technique 8: low-angle hero 0.2 m, -14 deg. To push without a lunge, use an anchor with a second beat at dist 0.8.

shots.name: High angle (diminish)
shots.purpose: Camera above, looking down on one fighter: small, exposed, losing.
shots.when: The struck fighter, the moment of doubt, after a disarm.
shots.angle: -20 (negative for the foe: keeps the same side of the line)

shots.name: Blade slide (arm to guard)
shots.purpose: Camera travels along the arm, elbow to wrist to tsuba, then holds on the guard.
shots.when: The draw, the grip change, the 'weapon as a character' beat.
shots.notes: Motion-page beat: t and until are absolute seconds (add your start). Main-engine fallback: the blade rig (rides the drawn blade; falls back to a frame rig when no blade frame).

shots.name: Draw macro (blade rider)
shots.purpose: Lens rides just above the blade as it leaves the scabbard: steel fills the frame.
shots.when: Iai draw, the studio 'sword as a character' beat.
shots.notes: Sound: koiguchi click (-100 ms) -> slide -> tip-clear shing (docs/FIX-LIST.md).

shots.name: Eye to blade (rack-focus feel)
shots.purpose: Start on the eyes, slide down the arm to the blade: attention moves from intent to instrument.
shots.when: Just before the first strike; the 'look, then the sword answers' beat.
shots.engine: approx: a true rack focus needs depth of field (BokehPass planned, docs/FIX-LIST.md item 10); today the camera slides instead
shots.notes: When DOF lands: hold framing, pull focus from eye (0.6 m) to tsuba (0.9 m) over 8-12 frames.

shots.name: Blade glint insert
shots.purpose: Tight on the edge as a star of light runs along it.
shots.when: 4-6 frames before contact, or as the hook's first frame.
shots.engine: approx: the glint effect itself is planned (research/anime-fight-craft.md section 5 item 7)
shots.notes: [C] Demon Slayer analysis: a glint warns of the strike, then light shapes and sparks.

shots.name: Lunge dolly two-shot
shots.purpose: Clean three-quarter two-shot that follows a cut or lunge with a slight lag.
shots.when: Default coverage for a strike exchange.
shots.notes: Default behaviours on. 9:16 rig uses angle 55 (depth staging); 16:9 keeps 22.

shots.name: Torpedo chase track
shots.purpose: Camera rides behind and beside a dashing fighter, looking ahead of them.
shots.when: Tsuki dash, charge, a run across the set.

shots.name: Leading track (face the charge)
shots.purpose: Camera backs away in front of a charging fighter: they come at the lens.
shots.when: The decisive charge, a run at the viewer, the hook.
shots.notes: Torpedo spring overshoots ~8%: the fighter gains on the lens, which is the point. Guard keeps 0.8 m minimum.

shots.name: Whip reveal
shots.purpose: A very fast swing of view from one fighter to the other, ending on the threat.
shots.when: Answer to an attack, a surprise arrival, an off-screen strike.
shots.engine: approx: real whip pans need motion blur (planned); the torpedo spring gives the snap
shots.notes: Beat t relative to the shot start. Best used as a CUT point: cut on the fastest frame of the whip (docs/FIX-LIST.md technique 4).

shots.name: Handheld clash
shots.purpose: Loose, nervous framing on a blade-to-blade clash.
shots.when: Parry, block, the first contact.
shots.notes: Handheld is a spice: at most 1 in 4 shots, never on the standoff.

shots.name: Dutch bind
shots.purpose: Tilted close two-shot on crossed blades and straining faces.
shots.when: Blade lock (tsubazeriai), the struggle beat.
shots.notes: docs/FIX-LIST.md asks 12-18 deg for a bind; KUROKO clamps roll at +-10, so 10 is the current maximum. Switch the roll sign when the advantage switches.

shots.name: Stagger Dutch
shots.purpose: The frame tilts as a fighter reels back.
shots.when: Stagger, a heavy hit taken, losing balance.

shots.name: Jump-back reveal
shots.purpose: Camera pulls back and rises as a fighter leaps away: shows the space surrendered.
shots.when: Jump-back, retreat, dodge.

shots.name: Glide around the strike (3D-set orbit)
shots.purpose: Fast, smooth arc around the strike: the 3D space turns while the action stays centred.
shots.when: A signature move, a breathing-style technique, one per fight.
shots.notes: [C] ufotable: 2D characters inside 3D-built environments so the camera can move freely; action kept near frame centre. Our version: keep the subjects centred, move the world. Orbiting the striker (target) keeps them centred; orbiting the midpoint of two fighters at radius < 4 m loses one of them (found in testing). A continuous arc may cross the profile without breaking the 180-degree rule because the viewer sees the move.

shots.name: Itano dive
shots.purpose: Camera flies through the action close to a fast body, wide lens, with trails crossing the frame.
shots.when: A flurry of thrown blades, paper shards or a multi-strike burst. Rare.
shots.engine: approx: the many-projectile trails are not built; the camera part works
shots.notes: [C] Itano circus: many fast projectiles on crossing 3D paths with trails, camera flying among them (fan sources only).

shots.name: Wide action hold (no cut)
shots.purpose: A full-figure frame held through 2-4 moves so the choreography reads as real.
shots.when: A sequence of 3+ strikes that is good enough to show whole.
shots.distance: full, both bodies head to toe
shots.notes: [C] Stahelski: block with the camera, wide shot then dolly in, fewer cuts. Only for choreography that holds up at full body.

shots.name: One-take exchange (Spielberg-style oner)
shots.purpose: One continuous shot that becomes a two-shot, a close and a wide by moving, not cutting.
shots.when: The decisive exchange or a long build where cuts would break tension.
shots.notes: Beat t relative to the shot start. [C] Spielberg oners: blocking delivers the angles that would otherwise need cuts. Each beat should be a composition you would accept as its own shot.

shots.name: Hong Kong double hit (cut pair)
shots.purpose: Show one big hit twice: end shot A on the contact, start shot B 2-4 frames before it from 30+ degrees away.
shots.when: The biggest non-final hit, at most twice per film.
shots.engine: approx: the body timeline cannot rewind per shot yet; approximate by placing the cut 1-2 frames after contact and replaying the impact flash
shots.notes: [C] Hong Kong cutting holds shots long enough to feel the rhythm (pause-burst-pause, Bordwell); the overlapping 'hit twice' cut is commonly reported.

shots.name: Impact zoom (crash zoom)
shots.purpose: Snap the lens tighter in 2-frame steps on the hit: 34 -> 24 -> 16.
shots.when: The decisive blow, or the first clash. Once or twice per film.
shots.engine: approx: frame-fill moves the camera back as fov shrinks; a true zoom (fixed position) needs a keyframe shot. Keyframe version: same pos, fov 34/24/16 at t, t+2f, t+4f, ease linear
shots.notes: Beat t relative to shot start; put the first beat on the impact frame. docs/FIX-LIST.md technique 6. Add a shakes entry (amp 0.012-0.015) at the same t; KUROKO adds its own 7 deg punch.

shots.name: Impact close-up
shots.purpose: Close two-shot locked on the contact point exactly on the hit frame.
shots.when: Every important hit (keyframe on the hit second).
shots.notes: Pair with a shakes entry; hit-stop 3-4 frames. Do NOT frame two .hand points: the hand-to-hand axis flips during a strike and the camera jumps across the line (found in testing).

shots.name: Orbit through the hit-stop
shots.purpose: While bodies freeze on contact, the camera keeps moving around them: time stops, space doesn't.
shots.when: The decisive contact only (needs hit-stop on the motion page).
shots.engine: approx in the main engine: hit-stop freezes bodies only on the motion page today
shots.notes: docs/FIX-LIST.md technique 9. Motion-page orbit progresses until the END of the film, so put it last or keep the sweep small.

shots.name: Ink impact frame
shots.purpose: One frame: washi-white page, fighters as flat ink silhouettes, a red streak along the cut.
shots.when: The decisive contact; at most 1-2 per film.
shots.engine: ready on the motion page (effects.impactFrame); not a camera move: keep the current shot's rig
shots.notes: [C] Impact frames: 1 to a few frames of extreme value contrast at contact (Demon Slayer analysis credits Nozomu Abe). Set film.effects.impactFrame = true.

shots.name: Frozen pass hold (delayed reaction)
shots.purpose: Both fighters frozen after passing each other, backs turned; nothing moves for a long beat, then one falls or the paint blooms.
shots.when: Right after the decisive blow.
shots.notes: [C] Sanjuro's final duel: a long stillness (reported 20-36 s) before one sudden cut. For Shorts: 1.5-3 s of silence + wind only, then the paint (KIZU onset 80-200 ms).

shots.name: Zanshin orbit
shots.purpose: Slow arc around the winner holding the finishing posture.
shots.when: After the decisive cut, 1-2 s of zanshin before chiburi or noto.
shots.notes: As in film/motion-test.json. [C] Zanshin: alert posture held after the technique.

shots.name: Crane out to the end card
shots.purpose: Rise and pull back over the scene, leave the fighters small.
shots.when: Final 2-3 s before the end card.

shots.name: Walk away (back to camera)
shots.purpose: Follow the survivor from behind as they walk off into the light.
shots.when: Ending; the winner leaves, the loser stays in frame.

shots.name: Sky tilt (Shinkai light)
shots.purpose: Tilt up off the figures into the sky, sun or lantern-light rays.
shots.when: Transition out of a scene, a passage of time, the last beat before the title.
shots.notes: [C] Shinkai: lens flares, god rays, light as the subject. Needs a bright sky element in frame (paper sun in the dawn set).

shots.name: Graphic match cut (Satoshi Kon)
shots.purpose: End shot A on a shape (glowing eye), start shot B on the same shape in the same screen place and size (the lantern sun).
shots.when: Hook -> world, scene -> scene, memory -> present.
shots.notes: [C] Kon's transitions: general match cut, exact graphic match, intercutting mirrored times (Every Frame a Painting). The match is about screen position: check both stills and line the shapes up within ~5% of frame width.

shots.name: Hook flash-forward (0-1 s)
shots.purpose: The first second of the Short shows the most violent frame (impact or ink frame), then cuts back to the eye.
shots.when: Always: the first 0.4-1.0 s of every Short.
shots.notes: docs/FIX-LIST.md opening: 0-0.4 s ink impact frame -> 0.4-1.0 s eye close-up -> whip match-cut. [C] Shorts: viewers decide within ~1 s; start mid-action.

shots.name: Foreground wipe (kuroko cloth)
shots.purpose: Something dark passes very close to the lens (a sleeve, a kuroko cloth, a pine) and the cut hides inside it.
shots.when: Invisible cuts in a 'one-take', change of scene.
shots.engine: needs engine: no foreground-object rig yet (docs/FIX-LIST.md technique 7)
shots.notes: Kurosawa used screen wipes as transitions [C]; this is the in-camera cousin.

shots.name: Cut on action (match on motion)
shots.purpose: Cut mid-swing from one angle to another (>= 30 deg change) so the motion carries the eye across the cut.
shots.when: Every cut inside an exchange.
shots.engine: ready: it is an editing rule (choose shot start/end on the fastest frame)
shots.notes: [C] 30-degree rule avoids jump cuts; Kurosawa tends to cut on movement (Every Frame a Painting).

shots.name: Drift and smear (Wong Kar-wai)
shots.purpose: Handheld medium where the body moves in stutter (step-printed) while the background streaks.
shots.when: A memory, a dream fight, a moment of time distortion.
shots.engine: approx: step-printing = body poses on 3s/4s with camera on 1s; needs a render option for stepped body time
shots.notes: [C] Wong + Doyle: undercranking + step printing (e.g. shoot 12 fps, print each frame twice).

styles.summary: Action centred in frame, smooth glides through a 3D world, stepped body motion with smooth camera, glint -> strike -> sparks, colour-coded light.

cut_rhythm.pattern: long prepare (1-2 s) / single-frame strike / long relax (1-2 s); ~5 attacks per 8 s in a flurry

camera.shake: on ones over twos, kicked in the strike direction

styles.colour: deep blue-teal night, warm amber blade light, gold sparks; crimson only for the demonic side
effects: ink impact frame on the decisive hit
water/flame-like paper ribbon along the technique
styles.sound: silence before the technique name / strike, then a big layered clash

styles.summary: Erratic, mobile camera with a strong sense of 3D space; heavy blows; spatial continuity over abrupt cuts.

cut_rhythm.pattern: bursts of 3-5 short shots, then one 2-3 s moving take that shows where everyone is

styles.colour: desaturated base, saturated power colour (amber or crimson) on hits
styles.sound: punchy, lots of low-mid weight on hits

styles.summary: Moving weather in every frame, long lenses compressing layers, cuts on movement, long stillness then one violent instant.

cut_rhythm.pattern: long holds; cut on movement; the decisive blow is one short shot inside a very long still one

styles.colour: monochrome or near-monochrome; Ghost of Tsushima 'Kurosawa Mode' style grade with grain
styles.sound: wind bed loud, music absent; one sound for the cut

styles.inspired_by: Sergio Leone (The Good, the Bad and the Ugly)
styles.summary: Extreme wide vs extreme close-up; the standoff tightens toward the eyes on every cut while the cuts get shorter.

cut_rhythm.pattern: accelerating: 3.0, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.7, 0.5 s ... then the shot, then a long hold

styles.sound: music swells with the cutting, cuts to silence on the strike

styles.summary: Centred, symmetric, one-point compositions and slow, mechanical moves; dread through order.

cut_rhythm.pattern: few cuts, each one a hard jolt

effects: none, or a single impact frame

styles.summary: Step-printed stutter motion with continuous camera, handheld intimacy, saturated colour, time stretched.

cut_rhythm.pattern: lingering; stutter slow-mo on the key moment

styles.sound: one song carries the whole sequence

styles.inspired_by: Denis Villeneuve / Roger Deakins (Sicario, Blade Runner 2049)
styles.summary: Few sources, big negative space, silhouettes, slow deliberate moves, composition that lets the dark do the work.

cut_rhythm.pattern: patient; the threat is felt before it is seen

styles.colour: one dominant hue per scene (amber haze or cold blue), black shadows

styles.summary: One moving take that finds wide, two-shot and close through blocking; invisible.

cut_rhythm.pattern: one take per dramatic unit; cut only when the story turns

styles.inspired_by: Sword of the Stranger (Bones, action director Yutaka Nakamura)
styles.summary: Bodies fly and the camera flies with them; luminous blade arcs; terrain (snow) bursting with each move; no dialogue in fights.

cut_rhythm.pattern: fluid runs of 2-3 s with the camera following, punctuated by 2-4 f impact shots

styles.colour: cold white/blue world, amber blade light
effects: paper-snow bursts on footwork and impacts
styles.sound: no score under the fight; steel and breath

styles.summary: Break-dance swordplay, cuts and transitions on turntable scratches, beats with abrupt endings.

cut_rhythm.pattern: on the music grid: cut on beats, a scratch = a rewind/repeat cut

styles.summary: Light is the subject: lens flares, god rays, bloom, drifting clouds; quiet camera, sky tilts.
styles.colour: saturated dawn: gold, pink, deep sky blue

styles.summary: Every scene change is a match: shape, position, motion or time mirrored across the cut.

cut_rhythm.pattern: each cut lines up a shape in the same screen place

styles.lighting: any (match the two sides of the cut)
styles.colour: match colour across the cut too
styles.sound: carry a sound across the cut (J/L cut)

styles.summary: Many fast projectiles on crossing curved paths with trails; the camera dives among them.

cut_rhythm.pattern: one long dive, then a hard cut to the result

effects: thrown blades / paper shards with ribbons (planned)
styles.sound: layered whooshes panned by screen position

styles.summary: 3D sets with painted projection, hand-directed light and colour per shot, 2D effects over 3D bodies.

cut_rhythm.pattern: classic coverage; style lives in light and texture

styles.colour: complementary pairs per scene (amber vs teal), painted gradients

styles.inspired_by: Hong Kong action (Jackie Chan, Sammo Hung; Bordwell's pause-burst-pause)
styles.summary: Hold the shot long enough to feel the rhythm; pause-burst-pause; show a big hit twice.

cut_rhythm.pattern: pause (0.5-1 s still) / burst (3-6 moves in one shot) / pause

styles.summary: Wide, full-body frames and long takes so the viewer believes the performer does the fight; colour-saturated low light.

styles.summary: 15-25 s voice-led Short: 70% darkness, one shaft of light, strong rim, glowing eye ECU, slow push 2-5%/s, one decisive gesture, cut to black + small logo.

beatCamera._about: Which camera for which action beat (docs/STUDIO-STANDARD.md §3a). 'compose' = motion-page beat (film.camera, cameraOpts.solver 2); 'kuroko' = the closest main-engine rig.

calm.camera: over the shoulder towards the target, slow push-in

dash.camera: side track at knee height with lead room; arc to the front during the slow motion

compose._note: az is world degrees: 90 off the direction of the run

turn.camera: start behind, end over the shoulder; dolly-zoom for the realisation

jump-apex-slash.camera: during the slow motion, circle from below to above and behind, over the shoulder into the cut

landing.camera: low, wide, from the front, handheld settle

zanshin.camera: slow arc, crane up, push in
